## Verdict: Needs changes before merge

Reviewed head `532d0fa92` (PR #3471), trial-merged with `origin/main` `6e641dac7` in a local review worktree (rationale only, no code change: merge commit `134f1ca81`, no conflicts). Main moved past the earlier trial merge (the Agie-native merge changed `crates/geometry`), so this is a fresh merge. Built locally only; no runner. No code defect was found. One process item blocks a "ready" verdict: the reached heavy lanes did not run (see below), and "not run" is never a pass.

## What looks good

- The law is checked on the words as written, not on stream millimetres. `arcFateOf` (`crates/post/src/post/arc_guard.rs:44`) compares the script's own `word(k, v)` for the in-plane ends, and `short_arc_on_lattice` (`crates/post/src/post/cnc_arc_lattice.rs:32`) compares micrometre words. The tolerance is the output resolution, not an arbitrary epsilon. The old `1e-5 mm` bands in `tinyg.cps` and `heidenhain.cps` are removed and replaced with exact-equality or geometry checks.
- The `linear` fallback cannot move the tool sideways. `arcFate` returns `linear` only when the written in-plane ends coincide and the plane-normal (helix) or a rotary word moves. The post then calls its own `onLinear()`, which writes the same `wo(..., orgX/Y/Z)` word the guard compared (for example `assets/posts/fanuc.cps:249-250`, `doosan-dnm.cps:287-289`). The written in-plane end equals the current-position word, so only the helix or rotary word changes. `none` writes no motion block. The only path error is below one output unit, which is the intended trade.
- The near-full-turn exemption is safe. With coincident written ends and a true sweep over half a turn, the full circle is what the control reads; for that case the chord is tiny, so the radius and the extra arc length are both sub-resolution.
- The stream writer (`crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs:371-372`) keeps a stated full turn (`s[u]==e[u] && s[v]==e[v]`) and a near-full turn (`sweep > PI`) as arcs, and writes only the short case as a `Feed`. That fixes the defect at the source that still knows the true sweep (the reporter's 0.09 um R50 fillet no longer posts `G02 ... I0. J-50.`).
- Safety law: no `unwrap/expect/panic!` in the changed Rust; the numeric casts are guarded; a centreless arc is left to the script's named refusal. Provenance lines on both new modules. No golden, snapshot, `CHANGELOG.md` or process-file edits. Body has a `Changelog:` line and ends with `Fixes #3442`; subjects are conventional.

## Results merged with main (local)

- Post crate, every test binary in the diff's quick plan: 112 gate steps green (the `cargo xtask gate quick` post build and all post suites), 0 failed. Directly by name: `coincident_arcs` 8 passed, `cnc_arc_lattice` 2 passed, `radius_arcs` 7 passed.
- App suites by name (green): `between_setups` 10, `bore_cycle` 4, `carvera_post` 4, `conformance` 7, `control_comp` 5, `golden_cl` 33, `grblhal_post` 9, `klartext_builtin` 3, `lathe_post` 7, `lathe_post_inch` 6, `lathe_post_tormach` 8, `linuxcnc_post` 9, `mach4_builtin` 2, `microarc_test_part` 4, `plasma_post` 5, `post_unit_word` 5, `posting` 17, `short_arc_lattice` 2, `sodick_wire_post` 8, `tinyg_post` 18, `tormach_post` 10, `wire_post` 12.
- Quick gate (`cargo xtask gate quick --base origin/main`): the post portion is fully green (112 steps, 0 fail). The app portion did not finish: the app test-binary build (step 113) stalled in the shared `sccache` wrapper (the processes sat at 0 % CPU) because two other PR reviews were building on the same machine. I stopped it and ran the 22 touched app suites above by name instead. The other ~130 app suites of the quick plan were not run.
- Clippy: `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` is clean (exit 0; only the pre-existing workspace `truck-polymesh` manifest warning).

## Mutation check (the pin can go red)

I disabled the stream-writer conversion in `crates/post/src/post/cnc_arc_lattice.rs` (`sweep <= PI` made always false) and ran the app pin `a_sub_micrometre_fillet_posts_no_full_circle_through_the_whole_job_path`. It FAILED, as it must:

```
inch=false: full circles ["G02 X10.346 Y-2.98 Z2.5 I0. J-50. F800"]
```

I restored the file byte for byte (blob `b30598f716ba55eab85c2f0f1394c9dd4281c77e`, clean `git status`) and the pin is green again (2 passed). The pin really guards the fix.

## Heavy lanes

The diff reaches the heavy set: `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main --dry-run` lists 207 steps (post reaches every app heavy lane). The author did not run them (the PR body says "Heavy lanes ... not run yet"), and this review did not run them either: a cold release build of the 207 steps cannot complete while the machine is saturated by the two other reviews building. So the reached heavy lanes are **not run** - not a pass. This is the one item before merge (AGENTS.md "Heavy lanes at review").

## Requested before merge

1. Run `cargo xtask gate heavy --base origin/main` on head `532d0fa92` and name the reached lanes and their results in the PR body before the PR is flagged ready. No code change is requested; the 207 reached app heavy steps must be green first. If any linked light twin is red, run the matching full heavy step too.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs:465`: `Record::Thread(..)` neither updates nor clears `pos`, while `Touch`/`Retreat`/`Guard` clear it. A `Move` arc that followed a thread record with no move between would use a stale start. It is not reachable in the app's record order (a move always precedes an arc), but a reset there would match the probe handling.
- `crates/post/src/post/cnc.rs` is ~1064 lines before this PR; the change adds ~23 lines to a file already over the ~400-line target. Not blocking; a later split along the record seam would help.
- `crates/post/tests/coincident_arcs.rs` is 425 lines, close to the ~400-line target for a new test file.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
